_about: Authored words for the endpoint lab's SECTION MAP tab — the card's eleven ruled blocks (prisms-endpoint.json, D-015) laid beside the lab surface that answers each one. The tree, the attributes and every count are GENERATED (gen-endpoint-facts.py reads the brain map's own committed tree, which is m1-cluster.js's homes, self-proven at its generation). Nothing numeric is typed here: {tokens} are filled by the generator. The JOIN below is a PROPOSAL — authored words, never a measurement — and the page says so on its face. A block's pairing is one of THREE kinds (D-022): a page (a surface on the bench answers it) · no page yet (nothing does, and the gap is what the next piece should build) · a running header (it belongs to every part: it is lit where the part draws its stage reading, and on every other part its row names the gap for that part). Plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode and are checked by plain-audit.py.

tab.note: the card's {nBlocks} ruled blocks against the lab surface that answers each one — a page, no page yet, or a running header across every part. Clicking a block moves the bench; moving the bench lights the block. Lab chrome — none of it ships with the console.

head.title: section map
head.sub: {nBlocks} blocks · {nAttrs} attributes · {nWithSurface} with a page, {nWithoutSurface} with no page yet, {nHeader} a running header
head.lede: The ruled shape of the endpoint card, beside what the bench draws for it today.
head.proposal: The pairing of a block to a lab surface is AUTHORED, not measured — it is a proposal, and the rows with no page yet are the ones the next piece should build.

strings.sharedNote: An attribute three or more blocks need belongs to none of them, so it is listed under each as shared.
strings.leadLab: the bench moved and this lit
strings.absent: The card's ruled tree was not read, so nothing is drawn here.
strings.staleNote: The brain map's committed tree was built from an older inventory, so the blocks below may not match the ruling.
strings.feedbackWhat: a note about what you are looking at
strings.feedbackHint: the bench's state, the block it answers and the gap between them, ready to paste back with your words under it
strings.headerNone: has no stage reading yet, so the stages cannot be read on this part — you are still on it.
strings.foldTip: shows or hides this block's fields, and moves nothing

lines: A block is a group of the {nQuestions} questions, ruled by hand; the {nBlocks} groups are the ruling D-015.
An attribute's home is the block its use weighs into most, and one that three or more blocks need is shared and homed nowhere.
The tree is read from the brain map's committed page, whose own generator proves its home rule against m1-cluster.js on every run.

acts.part: opens that part on the bench
acts.variant: opens that part and switches it to the distribution that draws the block
acts.exit: picks an ending, so every part is projected onto it
acts.path: picks a whole route and draws its record in the portrait
acts.none: moves nothing and names what would have to be built, because no page answers it
acts.header: stays on the part you are on and shows its stage reading, or says this part has none yet

join._about: Keyed by the block's QUESTION SIGNATURE, which is prisms-endpoint.json's own key and survives a reorder. Every signature must appear here or the generator stops. `act` is parsed: part:<k> · part:<k>/<variant> · exit · path · none · header. A `header` entry carries `readings` — {part: the variant that is that part's stage reading} — and every part it does not name has no stage reading yet.

Q1+Q2+Q9.says: The Data panel draws every table the endpoint touches, the operation on each, and the fate of the writes at the end.
Q1+Q2+Q9.gap: Provisions — what a dependency's own commit leaves behind — is carried in the feed and drawn nowhere.
Q1+Q2+Q9.plain: Tables the endpoint reads and writes, with the fate of each change.

Q3+Q11.says: The command panel holds one cell per way the request ends, and picking one projects every part onto that ending.
Q3+Q11.plain: Every way the request can end, and the one it is expected to take.

Q5+Q7.says: The stage spine runs across every part — Data draws it as stage blocks today, and the other parts have no stage reading of their own yet.
Q5+Q7.gap: Only Data has a stage reading, so on every other part the header says so instead of jumping to Data.
Q5+Q7.plain: Stations a request passes, in the order they run.

Q4.says: The Tests panel stacks the cases by the status they assert and names the conditions nothing reaches.
Q4.plain: Conditions a test proves, and the ones nothing reaches.

Q6+Q17.says: The Security panel draws the app band, this endpoint's own guards and the gate among them, in run order.
Q6+Q17.gap: Deciding branches and catches — the forks one call down — ride the path portrait instead of this panel.
Q6+Q17.plain: Checks that stop a request, and the forks that decide its ending.

Q10+Q13.says: The Schemas panel draws the request body and the response body as blocks, every field a mark of its declared kind.
Q10+Q13.gap: Response headers per ending are in the feed and appear on no schema block.
Q10+Q13.plain: Shape of the body that comes in, and the body that goes out.

Q15+Q18+Q19.says: The Functions panel draws the handler and the call tree behind it, each function marked by what it decides and touches.
Q15+Q18+Q19.plain: Code that runs behind the endpoint, sorted by how much it decides.

Q16.says: The portrait's path record names everything alive while the request runs, but only once a route is picked.
Q16.gap: No part gives it a home — the path record carries it only once a route is picked, which is a workaround, not a home.
Q16.plain: Values alive while the request runs, and how long each one lasts.

Q12.says: The Security panel carries the idempotency claim and the delivery fact as one-line rows, and hover cards say how common a piece is.
Q12.gap: It compares this endpoint against the others, and no part does that — nothing lays the shared machinery beside what only this endpoint does.
Q12.plain: Machinery this endpoint shares with the rest of the app, against what only it does.

Q14+Q20.says: The head bar names the endpoint and flies the risk flag, and the command panel counts the findings behind one cell.
Q14+Q20.gap: No panel gathers the overview — coverage per condition, the findings themselves, the endpoint's place in the app and the outside services it calls have no surface.
Q14+Q20.plain: The whole endpoint at a glance — size, findings, and the place it sits in the app.

Q8.says: The Widening panel draws the screens that fetch this endpoint and the ladder from the endpoint out to the app.
Q8.gap: Whether the client can tell the endings apart is measured in the feed and drawn on no rung.
Q8.plain: Screens that call this endpoint, and what they do with each answer.
